terms.meaning: a library for building web page parts that update when their data changes
a built-in React function that lets a part remember values or run code when it appears or changes
a drawing format made of shapes and lines that stays sharp at any size
a plain text format for structured data

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Component setup and imports
sections.what: Marks this as a browser-only part and loads the React tools and the helper that builds asset paths.
sections.why: The diagram measures the page and reads the browser, so it must run in the browser.

sections.name: StackNode
sections.title: Shape of one technology box
sections.what: Describes a single box: its id, name, layer, and role.
sections.why: Gives every box the same shape so the drawing code can rely on it.
sections.watch_out: The role value must match a key in the role label table or it will show as a raw code.

sections.name: StackGraph
sections.title: Shape of the whole stack file
sections.what: Describes the full file: source note, layers, boxes, links, and AI features.
sections.why: Defines what the stack file must contain.
sections.watch_out: A file that lacks these fields can break the drawing rather than show a message.

sections.name: Line
sections.title: Shape of one drawn link
sections.what: Describes one line: its two ends, an optional label, its curve path, and the point where its label sits.
sections.why: Stores the calculated drawing data for each link.

sections.name: ROLE_NOTE
sections.title: Plain labels for role codes
sections.what: Converts internal codes such as web, db, or model into short readable labels shown under each box.
sections.why: Keeps the stack file short while showing readable text on screen.
sections.watch_out: A code missing from this table shows its raw code instead.

sections.name: CodeGraph (part 1)
sections.title: Loading the stack file and measuring boxes
sections.what: Fetches the stack file for the project, tracks box positions and hover state, and tracks whether the file is missing.
sections.why: The alive flag stops a late fetch from updating the page after the project has changed.
sections.watch_out: Changing the slug triggers a new fetch, so the cleanup must stay in place to avoid stale data.

sections.name: CodeGraph: for
sections.title: Calculating the curved lines
sections.what: Measures each box and works out a curved path for every link. Links between boxes in the same column bow out to the right.
sections.why: Without the bow, links between boxes in one column would cut straight through other boxes.
sections.watch_out: Measurements read screen positions, so they must run after the boxes are drawn.

sections.name: CodeGraph (part 3)
sections.title: Drawing the frame, lines, and boxes
sections.what: Draws the frame, the technology count, the lines, and the grid of boxes. Hovering or focusing a box highlights its links and dims the rest.
sections.why: Hover and keyboard focus both trigger the highlight, so the diagram works without a mouse.
sections.watch_out: Lines are hidden on small screens, so phone visitors see only the boxes.

sections.name: CodeGraph (part 4)
sections.title: AI features list and source note
sections.what: Shows the list of AI features and the source note under the diagram.
sections.why: Lists the AI features separately from the drawing.
sections.watch_out: The feature list is hidden when it is empty.

summary: Draws a diagram of the technologies in one project, arranged in columns by layer, with curved lines showing how they connect.
purpose: Shows the architecture of a project on its detail page, using the data in that project's stack file.
why: Lets a visitor see how the parts of a build fit together without reading code.
how: Loads the project's `stack.json` file, measures where each box sits on screen, draws curved lines between linked boxes, and highlights the links of whichever box the pointer or keyboard focus is on.
inputs: A project slug, which selects the file at the project's media folder. The stack file holds layers, technology boxes, links, and a list of AI features.
outputs: A grid of technology boxes with connecting lines, a count of technologies and links, and an AI features list. If the file is missing, a 'coming soon' box is shown instead.
risks: Line positions depend on measured box positions, so they must be recalculated when the page resizes. A stack file that does not match the expected shape can cause errors.
debug: If the 'coming soon' box shows, check that `stack.json` exists for that slug. If lines are in the wrong place, check the resize handling in `measure`. If a box is in the wrong column, check that its layer matches a layer id in the file. If a role shows as a raw code, add it to `ROLE_NOTE`.
